/kind regression

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Refactor locks on `GetNodeDetails` and `refreshNodes` calls.

This lock was blocking volume creation and destroying the ability to provision
volume with `thin` SC.

@Danil-Grigorev I looked into code and observed following. - GetNodeDetails holds the lock on `nm.registeredNodesLock.Lock()` - GetNodeDetails calls GetNodeInfoWithNodeObject() - GetNodeInfoWithNodeObject calls getRefreshedNodeInfo() - getRefreshedNodeInfo() calls RediscoverNode() when retrieved nodeInfo is nil - RediscoverNode() calls GetNode() - GetNode() needs `nm.registeredNodesLock.RLock()` Question is why getRefreshedNodeInfo() finds nodeInfo nil, I see only one writer for `nodeInfoMap`, which does not write nil `nodeInfo`. I checked callers of `addNodeInfo`, they do not write node name with nil `nodeInfo` in the nodeInfoMap so here we are retrieving node which is recently added but not present in the node manager. @Danil-Grigorev while volume is being provisioned, new node was being added to the k8s cluster. Asking this to understand the case when this is happening. I am trying to figure out why we received nil `nodeInfo` from the nodeInfoMap in `getRefreshedNodeInfo()`

I think we have a problem introduced when we merged - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90836 and what is happening is, when `GetNodeDetails` in `nodemanager.go` is called it acquires a lock on `registeredNodesLock`, but same function ends up calling `GetNode` which acquires another lock on `registeredNodesLock` object . Now the problem is, `GetNode` function gets called in a loop and it will try to acquire lock for each node it processes and hence two operations could result in deadlock.

This results into inability to provision a `PVC` with a default `thin` StorageClass. The volume does not get to call the API endpoint, just hangs after `CreateVolume` call, which is clear in the goroutine dump.

**What you expected to happen**:

1) Provision a `PVC` from `thin` `SC` successfully.
2) Don't be blocked by credentials secret change.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

1) Provision a vSphere cluster with credentials secret set
2) Create volume
3) Wait...

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.19.0-rc.2+5241b27-dirty
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: vSphere
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Linux
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): GNU/Linux
- Install tools: openshift-install (kubeadm)
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
comments: This should be a blocker bug for 1.19 at least as far as vsphere cloudprovider integration is concerned, because it breaks cloudprovider integration/volume provisioning. cc @andrewsykim

Something makes me think this issue existed before, and just escalated to a larger scope after adding `Secret` informers, demanding refresh for all `Node` objects. This [method](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5a3301a59d0c4d5e76002cff99a2f5450d2eea80/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/vsphere_util.go#L129) is used within `vsphere-volume` plugin in `kcm` and it is mounting the volume if it is required, calling  [nodeManager.GetNodeDetails()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5a3301a59d0c4d5e76002cff99a2f5450d2eea80/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/vsphere_util.go#L130) - it is locking on all the nodes at once. If the `kcm` pod was just restarted (say `leader-election` just changed, or the health probes demanded a restart), it would process all existing `Nodes` at the same time as trying to mount/create the volume. And both threads will clang on the same lock, as the `nodeInfo` would probably not be populated at that moment, so will go the path of [Discovery](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a36704b444518f1736f5f24197d007e642ffb66a/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/nodemanager.go#L432) - same which is used in [RegisterNode](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a36704b444518f1736f5f24197d007e642ffb66a/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/nodemanager.go#L233-L236). So we get lost volume data, pending `PVCs` etc... And the links I'm sharing are from `1.16` Kubernetes, where issues with similar footprint randomly arose.

review_comments: Should this be copying the nodes so that we don't mutate them later? Where is registered nodes updated, is this also done under lock?

`registeredNodes` returned from here are not updated in the workflow. 

I see in the `(nm *NodeManager) refreshNodes()` we are just iterating over the key `nodeName` and do not update the node object.

we can return copy of nodes instead of a pointer. This will require further refactoring as other methods in the workflow are accepting node pointer as argument.

@JoelSpeed Every operation with registeredNodes is now done under lock supervision, and none of them requires special isolation except the one provided by the defined operations like add or delete, which already locking the resource themselves for the further processing. Each resource operating on the node pointer will update the Node object under the pointer, which is the intent of the method - but will do this while locking the needed resource.

Just to clarify, what I meant was should we do `registerdNodes[nodeName] = node.DeepCopy()` which would return a copy that is still a pointer, it would be a very minor change that wouldn't need refactoring anywhere else.

If would seem like the point of this function is to create a copy of `nm.registeredNodes` so that outside actors aren't mutating the NodeManager's internal state, if we aren't doing a DeepCopy before returning the nodes, then outside actors can still modify the internal state.

Having looked at where this is used, the only thing we are actually using from the result of this function is the names of the objects anyway, so it is safe as it currently is, my concern would be if someone started using it to modify stuff later down the line.

It also looks like this could be simplified, we don't actually need the node object where it is being used, but that doesn't need to be addressed now.
